definitions.explanation: Describes food that has just been deep-fried and is still hot and crispy. Often used as a modifier with の.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げたての{天|てん}ぷらは{最高|さいこう}だ。
examples.english: Freshly fried tempura is the best.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げたてのコロッケを{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate a freshly fried croquette.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げたての{唐揚|からあ}げはサクサクしていてとてもおいしい。
examples.english: Freshly fried karaage is crispy and very delicious.

notes:
FORMATION:
Formed from {揚|あ}げる (to deep-fry) + たて (just done). The suffix たて attaches to the conjunctive form of verbs to mean "just [verb]ed."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {揚|あ}げたての{天|てん}ぷら (freshly fried tempura)
- {揚|あ}げたてのコロッケ (freshly fried croquette)
- {揚|あ}げたての{唐揚|からあ}げ (freshly fried karaage)

RELATED WORDS:
- {焼|や}きたて: freshly baked/grilled
- {炊|た}きたて: freshly cooked (rice)
- {出来|でき}たて: freshly made
